gaps: Only the LLC filing path is modelled step by step. The other filed structures (nonprofit corporation § 29-402.01, corporation § 29-302.01, professional corporation § 29-506, limited partnership § 29-702.01, LLP statement of qualification § 29-610.01) also go to the Mayor and fall under the same general filing duty and refusal procedure (§§ 29-102.01, 29-102.06), but their content checks and the moment each comes into existence (e.g. a limited partnership needs a general and a limited partner, § 29-702.01(c)) are not modelled.

No fee amount appears in these sections: § 29-102.12(a) leaves entity filing fees to the Mayor's rules, and the basic business license and trade name registration fees are not stated in the printed sections either. The fee outputs of business_structure therefore point to the rules rather than giving amounts.

§ 29-102.06(c) gives the Mayor 15 business days after delivery to return a refused filing, but says nothing about what follows if the Mayor neither files nor refuses in time; the deadline is marked 'unstated' and silence is not treated as a denial. Nor does the section set a time for filing an acceptable certificate.

The 60-day window in § 29-102.06(c) only affects the fee: a corrected filing within 60 days of the rejection is free; after that the entity may still refile but must pay. The missed window is therefore modelled as a late corrected filing that must pay the applicable fee again (on_miss rejoins collect_fee, then review_filing), not as a lapse of the right to file; the late corrected filing's own delivery is not drawn as a separate message, and a filer who never refiles is not modelled.

Court review (§ 29-102.06(d)) ends the model at the court's ruling; if the court orders the Mayor to file, the filing and acknowledgment that follow are not drawn as a rejoin to file_certificate. Whether the person may both refile and petition is not addressed; the model offers them as alternatives.

The LLC is formed only when the certificate is filed, becomes effective and at least one person becomes a member (§ 29-802.01(d)); membership and delayed effective dates are not modelled, so the acknowledgment of filing stands in for formation.

After filing, two independent obligations may apply: trade name registration (§ 47-2855.02, only for a business using a trade name) and the basic business license (§ 47-2851.02, for anyone doing business in the District, subject to the exemptions in subsection (h)). They are not mutually exclusive, but the flow conditions take one variable per step, so the model reaches the licence either directly or after the trade name registration through an exclusive gateway; it is correct only if the gateway evaluates uses_trade_name first, in document order. No printed section makes the licence depend on the trade name registration.

The basic business license exemptions (§ 47-2851.02(h): conventions, gross annual revenue of $2,000 or less with self-certification on request, charitable entertainments, cottage food products) are folded into the license_required condition rather than tested in a table. A licence is needed for each business location (subsection (c)); endorsements and the licence categories set elsewhere in subchapter I of Chapter 28 of Title 47 are not printed here and not modelled.

The Department's check that the applicant 'complies with all applicable District and federal laws and regulations' (§ 47-2851.02(b)) is a single condition (complies_with_law); what those laws require for a particular business (zoning, certificate of occupancy, tax registration, professional licensing) is outside these sections.

Beneficial ownership disclosure (§ 29-102.01(a)(6)-(9)) is stated for 'entity registration filings'; the model treats a certificate of organization as one, since an entity without the disclosure 'shall not be allowed to register or do business in the District' (§ 29-102.01(a)(8)).
Nonprofit corporation status is a District corporate form, not tax exemption; federal 501(c) status is outside the D.C. Code and not modelled.
Biennial reports and later filings are not modelled.
